I have loved this game dearly for years, and that's why I need to tell you to stay the hell away.

This game is beautiful. This game can be amazingly fun. But it is a cash grab of DLC, minimal bug fixes, and oh my GOD it is a storage hog. Every time they drop a new DLC (which is frequent, how else are they gonna sap your cash away?) you have to download it to your game, whether you are going to buy it or not. On one hand, this allows you to check out DLC if your friend/anyone on a public server is hosting a DLC reserve. 

On the other hand. As of time of writing this review, it is 109 GB. Red Dead Redemption 2 is 118 GB. HOW IN THE NAME OF HELL IS THIS GAME ONLY 9 GB LESS THAN RDR2? This game forces you to download every damn unoptimized DLC, and its just making it bloat more and more no matter how much I do not want to buy these damn guns or feeders.

If you have a ton of storage on your PC to burn? Hell, go for it, play the game. But wait for sales and use your money wisely, because there is so much DLC here that you can drain your coffers fast if you're not careful. Saw someone else say the game is ~310$ if you're paying full price for all the current DLC.

If you're like me and don't have 109 GBs to spare to a game that just keeps bloating, do not buy this game.

Imagine a world where there are no enemies shooting at you, no teammates yelling at you through voice chat, and no deadlines to meet. Just you, the majestic wilderness, and the gentle whispers of the wind between the trees.

This game is perfect for relaxation because:

~ Calming Audio & Visuals:
Realistic wilderness graphics with cinematic lighting and ambient sounds (wind, rain, water effects) that work like ASMR to soothe your stress.
~ Mindfulness Training:
The game forces you to slow down. Reading tracks, paying attention to the wind direction, and creeping through the wilderness feels like a meditative experience with minimal adrenaline but maximum satisfaction.
~ The Ultimate Solo Space:
The perfect place to disconnect from the chaos of the real world and enjoy the peaceful silence.

Put on your headphones, forget about your work stress for a bit, and let yourself get lost in the beauty of the wilderness.

Runs fine on my laptop, did not find it very engaging, but I just dont think the game was for me. Hard to tell if it's a good hunting game.

Unfortunately the game just isn't how I thought. It's my skill issue, not the game's fault. I can't find anything as easily as the Youtube tutorials make it seem. When I do find animals and shoot, they don't die. In fact they never die. 

I use adequate armament and ammo for the class, I stop for a while to let the character catch his breath, I'm inside the shooting distance I see on YT tutorials, hold breath, shoot lungs, the tracks show heavy bleeding, but they never die. It's the strongest deers in the world. I chase to the point of losing track, the blood trail disappears and they still aren't dead. They keep marching on. 4th time trying to get into this without success. I'm just trying to get any enjoyment out of the money I paid at this point. Again, it's my skill issue. I should have researched better. If you don't have any previous knowledge of hunting simulators / IRL hunting like me, your beginner experience could end up not being the most fun. Honestly I don't think I have the patience. I'll stick to modded RDR2 for hunting because that feels more arcade and more my speed. 

Now if you do know what you are doing, this game is beautiful and seems really immersive with the hunting experience. It looks very cool seeing somebody who knows what they are doing play it. I'd recommend it, if that's the case. I wish I could get into it.
